Get started with FunMel

Source: vignettes/FunMel.Rmd
FunMel.Rmd

FUNGAL CONFRONTATION ASSAYS

Photographs. Colony measurements. Matched controls.

Measure four approximately round Zymoseptoria tritici colonies around another fungus, retain their image provenance, and compare each treatment with its own experimental controls.

01 · Get started

Learn the objects, try a simulated plate, then prepare your photographs.

02 · Real photographs

Follow the complete eight-photo 14-day tutorial, including metadata, spot tables and exported figures.

03 · Every function

Explore the indexed function catalog for specialist calibration, training and measurement tools.

1. Install and load

Run installation once. After updating, restart R before loading the new package. In RStudio use Session → Restart R; other R applications can be closed and reopened. A loaded package should not be replaced in the same session.

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mghotbi/FunMel")
library(FunMel)
packageVersion("FunMel")
#> [1] '0.4.16'

R >= 4.1 and a source-compilation toolchain are required: Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS, matching Rtools on Windows, or R development tools and ImageMagick development libraries on Linux. To include locally installed vignettes, install with build_vignettes=TRUE, dependencies=TRUE:

remotes::install_github("mghotbi/FunMel",build_vignettes=TRUE,dependencies=TRUE)
vignette("FunMel",package="FunMel")
vignette("Real-14-day",package="FunMel")

2. See one plate before starting a project

This self-contained example uses a schematic image, not biological data. It shows the default arrangement: four target colonies and a central fungal partner.

sim <- simulate_plate(width=400,height=400,seed=1)
plate_result <- analyze_plate(sim$image,n_spots=3,spot_radius_mm=0.4,
                              n_boot=20,verbose=FALSE)
plate_result$colonies[,c("colony_id","detected","MI_mean","MI_spot_mean")]
#>   colony_id detected  MI_mean MI_spot_mean
#> 1        TL     TRUE 48.81529     45.58140
#> 2        TR     TRUE 52.99384     51.84266
#> 3        BR     TRUE 57.17307     57.43442
#> 4        BL     TRUE 41.43033     43.49997
plot_qc(plate_result)

Simulated plate: target-colony masks and central fungal core/hyphal-growth candidates.

Check the target outlines, central fungal tissue, connected hyphae and spot positions. These are image-based candidates, not species identifications or inhibition boundaries. The 20 bootstrap replicates keep teaching examples quick; they are not intended for precise uncertainty estimates.

For a control without a central fungus:

control_layout <- plate_layout(centre="none")
control_result <- analyze_plate(example_plate("control"),layout=control_layout,
                                max_dim=1200,n_boot=20)

Melanization index is MI = 100 − CIELAB L*. A larger value means darker pixels. It is an image-darkness proxy, not measured melanin concentration. Exposure, lighting, colour calibration and masks affect the measurement.

3. Choose the right starting point

What you have What to do
No data yet; you want to learn Continue with the real 14-day tutorial
A new photo ZIP Use prepare_experiment() and select the ZIP
A new folder of photographs Supply its full path, or select one original photo with prepare_experiment()
Several batches in nested folders Supply the common root folder or ZIP so every batch and its controls are included
Saved measurements from an earlier session Use load_experiment(); do not prepare the project again

A file chooser selects files, not folders. Selecting one original photograph uses its containing folder and subfolders; the package prints the exact folder it will scan. It includes all supported photographs there, not just the selected image. For multiple batches, select their ZIP or supply the common root folder path. Do not select a QC figure or metadata CSV as an original photograph.

New photographs: prepare once

Choose one of these alternatives:

project <- prepare_experiment() # Choose a photo ZIP or one original photo.
# Alternative: replace this example path with the common photo-folder root.
project <- prepare_experiment("/full/path/to/photos","FunMel_project")

Use a new output folder. An existing nonempty output is protected against replacement. If work is already saved, use the reopening instructions below.

Saved work: reopen and read 

project <- load_experiment() # Choose project.rds in its current project folder.
result <- read_experiment(project)
head(result$colonies)
head(result$spots)

Keep the complete project folder together when moving it. The loader reconnects internal paths. Original photographs outside that folder keep their external paths; they are needed for remeasurement, not for reading or finalizing saved measurements. project$result_file is a filename; result$spots is a table.

4. Check the experimental design 

project$metadata_file
metadata <- read.csv(project$metadata_file,check.names=FALSE)
metadata[,c("plate_id","set_id","treatment","centre_model")]
validate_metadata(metadata)

A unique plate_metadata.csv in the input is read automatically. Otherwise the package creates a template, proposing labels only for explicit structures such as batch1/control/ and batch1/fungus_A/. Folder names cannot prove biological assignments. Correct missing or inaccurate information using laboratory records before analysis.

Field Required interpretation
plate_id Globally unique independent plate, photographed once
file, relative_file Original image provenance; preserve the relative path
set_id Matching treatment and control group; controls are never borrowed from another set
treatment Exact label control for controls; consistent actual treatment labels otherwise
centre_model, partner_type none for controls, normally fungus for confrontation plates
day, medium, zymo_strain May be entirely unrecorded; once recorded, complete and constant within each set
Other fields Retained experimental annotations, including user-defined columns

For one control plus three treatment plates, enter four rows sharing a set_id; enter the control once. Four colonies per plate and multiple spots per colony are subsamples, not independent biological replicates. Repeated images of the same plate are not new independent replicates.

For a nested ZIP, relative paths distinguish identical basenames. Supply one combined metadata table with metadata= when there are multiple metadata files. Use control_folders="C" only when that exact label genuinely denotes controls.

5. Measure, inspect and finish 

dish_mm <- 90 # Replace with the verified outer diameter of your dishes (mm).
result <- run_experiment(project,dish_diameter_mm=dish_mm,max_dim=1200,
                         n_spots=5,spot_radius_mm=0.4)
result$analysis_status
result$failed
project$qc_dir

A completed run reports "complete" and zero failed images. Inspect every QC PNG for target masks, central fungal tissue/hyphae, spots, scale, lighting and warnings before interpretation. Informative QC warnings do not block the default workflow. Genuine failures still require correction; successful processing is not automatic biological validation.

The diameter must be an actual, finite positive measurement. All plates in one run use that setting; analyze different dish sizes separately. Omit n_spots and spot_radius_mm for whole-colony measurements only.

reviewed <- finish_experiment(project)
reviewed$melanization_coefficient
reviewed$assessment$status
print(plot_treatment_comparison(project))

Finalization reuses saved measurements and exports CSV tables, an assessment RDS, and a treatment comparison in PDF, SVG and 600-dpi PNG. Different recorded contexts are finalized into separate folders listed in context_index.csv.

6. Read the results correctly

Result Meaning
colonies / colonies.csv Whole-colony colour, area, MI and optional spot summaries
spots / spots.csv One row per achieved circular ROI, with coordinates and pixel summaries
profiles / profiles.csv Edge-to-centre darkness measurements
plates / plates.csv Plate-level detection, calibration and illumination status
metadata / metadata_used.csv Complete metadata with custom names and values retained
melanization_coefficient Set-specific treatment-to-own-control ratios
treatment_comparison_statistics.csv Means, SDs, counts and descriptive values plotted in the figure

Whole-colony MI_min, MI_mean and MI_max describe eligible interior pixels, excluding the rim and saturated/specular pixels. MI_spot_mean/min/max summarize individual spot means, not the darkest/lightest whole-colony pixels or confidence limits. Spot placement is deterministic, spatially spread and non-overlapping. Check n_spots_measured and spot_status; incomplete summaries are unavailable rather than invented.

The default coefficient divides the mean of treatment plate MI values by the mean of control plate MI values in the same set. Each plate averages its eligible target-colony MI means equally. Values above 1 indicate a darker image-based treatment mean, not a pigment-concentration fold change. Overall summaries weight set-specific ratios equally, rather than pooling all controls.

One control per set permits descriptive ratios but not the package’s replicated-cell significance tests. With adequate replication, assess_experiment() uses lme4/lmerTest, matched-set contrasts and Holm adjustment. Review model status, convergence, singularity, assumptions and experimental coverage before interpreting inference. The comparison plot itself is descriptive: bars show one between-plate SD, not confidence intervals; ratio SD conditions on the shared control mean and omits its uncertainty.

A prespecified, consistently applied spot-based descriptive analysis may use melanization_coefficient(reviewed,response="MI_spot_mean"). Keep that response separate from whole-colony MI.

7. Continue confidently

Message or situation Next step
Final outputs saved Finalization succeeded; read the exported tables and figure
Image QC unconfirmed Inspect masks, calibration and warnings; review before interpreting results
Insufficient plate replication Use descriptive results; do not interpret absent p-values as a software failure
Missing treatment or matching control Complete actual assignments; another batch’s control is not a substitute
Selected metadata CSV, PDF or SVG Reopen project.rds, or choose the original photo ZIP/photo
Output folder already exists Reopen its project.rds rather than preparing over saved work
Missing saved file Open the current complete project folder; restore genuinely missing files
Flat-field correction withheld Inspect illumination status; withholding does not demonstrate adequate lighting
Spots cannot fit Inspect masks and use consistent feasible spot settings across compared plates

Custom metadata is retained; measurement-name conflicts receive a metadata_ prefix only in measurement tables. The full metadata keeps original names. Changed segmentation layouts require reanalysis because the saved masks differ.

Next: work through the real photographs, explore every exported function, or read the installed guides/FunMel_overview.md for algorithms and use alongside ImageJ/Fiji.

Comparison captions are exported separately as treatment_comparison_caption.txt. Use caption="brief" or caption="full" in plot_treatment_comparison() to include a caption beneath the figure.
